6: # OpenAI Docs MCP Skill
7: 
8: ## Overview
9: 
10: Use the OpenAI developer documentation MCP server from the shell to search and fetch authoritative docs. Always do this for OpenAI platform work instead of relying on memory or non-official sources.
11: 
12: ## Core rules
13: 
14: - Always use this skill for OpenAI API/SDK/Apps/Codex questions or when precise, current docs are required.
15: - Query the MCP server via the CLI wrapper in `scripts/openai-docs-mcp.sh` (do not rely on Codex MCP tools).
16: - Use `search` or `list` to find the best doc page, then `fetch` the page (or anchor) for exact text.
17: - Surface the doc URL you used in your response so sources are clear.

19: ## Quick start

22: scripts/openai-docs-mcp.sh search "Responses API" 5
23: scripts/openai-docs-mcp.sh fetch https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses
24: ```

27:

29: 2. Read: `fetch` the most relevant URL (optionally add an anchor).

24: require_cmd() {

31: mcp_request() {

33:   curl -s -N \
34:     -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
35:     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
36:     -X POST "$MCP_URL" \
37:     -d "$payload" \

45:   local payload

47:     payload=$(jq -n --arg method "$method" '{jsonrpc:"2.0",id:1,method:$method}')
48:   else

51:   mcp_request "$payload"
52: }

125:        + (if ($cursor | length) > 0 then {cursor: $cursor} else {} end)')"
126:     resp="$(mcp_tool_call "list_openai_docs" "$args")"
127:     ensure_ok "$resp"

139:     resp="$(mcp_tool_call "fetch_openai_doc" "$args")"

144:     resp="$(mcp_tool_call "list_api_endpoints" "$(jq -n '{}')")"
